item.description: - A launchd job's detail now names its trigger next to the icon, such as Calendar, Interval or At Login. - The countdown to the next run is now headed by the date and time of that run, so you don't have to work it out. - New: Edit Schedule… is now also in the toolbar's More menu and the Item menu. - The Needs Attention section in the sidebar no longer shows a warning icon next to its title.

- New: hover over the speed and CPU charts, the storage bar or a launchd job's timeline to see the values right away — the time and speeds, the CPU of your Mac and the app at fault, a folder's size, or a scheduled, last or next run. - The CPU of your whole Mac is now shown as a share of all cores (0–100%), the same as Activity Monitor's System and User. Each app's CPU still uses 100% = one core. - Fixed: the network no longer warns about high latency when only the route to 1.1.1.1 is slow. Breaker now also pings 8.8.8.8 and uses the better result.

- New: System load. Breaker notifies you when one app keeps using the CPU (half a core or more on average for 10 minutes), when your Mac gets hot enough to slow its CPU, or when memory runs low. Short spikes such as a build don't count. The item shows which apps are using the CPU (100% = one core), when the app at fault started, and a 24-hour history. - New: Storage. Breaker notifies you when less than 10% of your startup disk is free. Every 6 hours it measures folders that tend to grow — Xcode DerivedData, simulators, caches, node_modules, npm and Gradle caches, and more — and shows what grew since the last scan on a bar of your disk. You can also scan now from the toolbar or the Item menu. No extra permissions are needed. - Copy Prompt for AI now works for the network, system load and storage items too, even when nothing is wrong, and has a new icon.

- New: launchd job details are now graphical. A big countdown to the next run, and a timeline of scheduled runs, the last run (✓/✗), missed runs and the next run. The timeline's width follows how often the job runs, from 15 minutes to a year. - Always-running (KeepAlive) jobs show their uptime and a band from when the process started. Jobs without a fixed schedule show their last run. - Symbols at the top right of the card show how each job is triggered: set times, interval, at login, file watch or always running. - Fixed: a process ID of four digits or more no longer shows a thousands separator.

- New: Network health. Breaker checks your connection, router, internet and DNS every minute, and notifies you only when the connection is down. The network item shows the route from your Mac to DNS, download and upload speed with a 7-day history, and Wi-Fi signal. - Speed is measured with macOS's built-in networkQuality, hourly by default (about 300 MB each). Choose the interval in Settings, or run it now from the toolbar or the Item menu. Automatic tests are skipped over a personal hotspot and in Low Data Mode. - Removed: SwiftBar plugins and monitored apps are no longer listed.

- New: Copy Prompt for AI. When a launchd or cron job fails, copy a prompt with the job's definition and recent log lines from the toolbar or the Item menu, and paste it into your AI assistant. - Log errors are now checked only in output written by the job's latest run.
- Lowered the minimum system requirement to macOS 26 (was macOS 27)
- An old error left in a job's log no longer marks it as failed again after Breaker restarts or updates. - A job that is working no longer shows an old log line as the cause of a failure.

- Schedule editor handles "every hour" times and hour ranges such as 7:00–23:00. They used to be removed when saving. - Logs follow new output while you're looking at them, and color codes no longer show up as garbage. - Shows a launchd job's environment variables, such as PATH. - An old error left in a log no longer marks a job as failed once it has run again. - Finds Folder Actions that use Automator workflows.

- First release. - Lists your launchd jobs, cron lines, Folder Actions, SwiftBar plugins, and the apps you choose, and notifies you when one breaks. - Signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple.
